target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — project Hays-local source pool lists O. calcicola. Burnet — documented wild population under former name Gaura calcicola along US 183. McCulloch — documented from Marshall Enquist's Wildflowers of the Texas Hill Country; current FNA places the species on Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos limestone.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county evidence only; historical Gaura/Calylophus names are counted only after synonym reconciliation.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the white-to-pink gaura-type flowers and limestone setting. Limestone gaura is a perennial from a woody rootstock, with narrow leaves and asymmetric 4-petaled flowers that open near sunset and fade dark pink to red.
diagnostic_traits: perennial clumped herb from twisted woody rootstock
4 unequal white petals fading dark pink/red
long-exserted style and stamens presented to one side
dry limestone, gypsum, or caliche habitat

comparisons.key_distinctions: O. filiformis is usually a robust winter annual/biennial with taller airy architecture; O. calcicola is perennial, limestone-associated, and has a woody rootstock.
